mechanism_narrative: A persistently depressed TRANSIT series keeps spontaneous shopping trips below baseline, and the small improvement in WORKPLACES is too weak to offset it. If transit mobility stays near or below the current level, RETAIL_REC remains lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean for the next 28 days despite TRANSIT remaining at or below -10% throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls further and crosses a sharper negative regime, retailers lose walk-in demand within one week because access frictions rise immediately. The mechanism predicts a short-lag decline in RETAIL_REC after a transit shock, with no such decline if transit does not breach that threshold.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15% week-on-week or stays below -15% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not drop within 7 days after TRANSIT crosses below -15%, or RETAIL_REC increases instead while transit remains below the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increases weekday exposure to shopping corridors and creates incremental retail trips after commute ends. When both series improve together, RETAIL_REC should trend upward over the following two weeks; if only one improves, the effect is too small to matter.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 14 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise relative to the current week.

mechanism_narrative: Higher RESIDENTIAL mobility proxies stay-at-home substitution, which suppresses discretionary retail visits with a delay of about four weeks. If residential time at home remains elevated, RETAIL_REC should underperform its prior 28-day mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above the current level.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in GROCERY_PHARM signals precautionary and necessity-focused trips that crowd out leisure retail in the near term. The more people shift toward essential shopping, the more RETAIL_REC weakens over the next two weeks; if grocery mobility falls back, the retail drag fades.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5%, or retail rises while grocery/pharmacy remains above -5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS use diverts discretionary time toward outdoor leisure and away from indoor retail spending. If PARKS mobility continues to improve from the current trough, RETAIL_REC should remain weaker over the next four weeks than over the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while PARKS also increases from the current week.

mechanism_narrative: Retail demand falls only when mobility restrictions hit both shopping access and commuting at the same time. A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES amplifies reduced retail exposure, producing a sharper decline in RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall below their current 4-week means by at least 2 percentage points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 14 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move below their current 4-week means by at least 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL also remains elevated, the population is substituting toward local outdoor activity and home-based routines rather than mall visits. That combination suppresses discretionary retail traffic, so RETAIL_REC should be lower over the next four weeks unless park mobility falls back quickly.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both stay at or above their current levels.
